WITH college_counts AS (
    SELECT college_id, COUNT(*) AS player_count
    FROM player_college
    GROUP BY college_id
), college_stats AS (
    SELECT AVG(player_count) AS all_colleges_avg,
           SUM(player_count) AS total_player_count
    FROM college_counts
), above_average AS (
    SELECT cc.player_count,
           cs.all_colleges_avg,
           cs.total_player_count
    FROM college_counts AS cc
    CROSS JOIN college_stats AS cs
    WHERE cc.player_count > cs.all_colleges_avg
)
SELECT AVG(player_count) AS above_average_colleges_avg_player_count,
       AVG(player_count * 1.0 / total_player_count) AS avg_fraction_of_total,
       AVG(player_count - all_colleges_avg) AS avg_excess_over_all_colleges_avg
FROM above_average

assumptions.assumption: Each row in player_college counts as one player-college record, including duplicate player records if present; NULL college_id values form one group. The total is the sum of these group counts, and averages are unrounded.
